lines.note: The first surviving line is a Portuguese continuation about women's vocabulary. The Paris copy jumps from printed page 109 to 112 here; no missing preceding text is invented.

runs.text: Couſa em que ſe poem acobertura,

lines.note: Futauoqi is a lid rest, literally a place to put a lid. Close-set acobertura is retained; the definition continues with the kind of lid below.

runs.text: ou teſto do caldeirão, ou panela do Chanoyu.

lines.note: The lid is that of the cauldron or pot used in Chanoyu. Chanoyu is italic within Portuguese here and remains so, with a typeface toggle available.
Futçǔ, explained Amanecu touoru, is the positive 'general/common' sense, corresponding to 普通. It contrasts with the negative homophone in the next entry.
Correct mir to the scan's mor, 'greater part'. Futçǔna fitode nai means not an ordinary person; its negation does not contradict the positive headword.

runs.text: Não he qualquer homem, ou dos ordi-

lines.note: The gloss says he is not just any man or one of the ordinary sort. Ordi- continues on the short line below.
Completes ordinarios. This physical continuation is preserved rather than merged into the preceding text.
The second Futçǔ is 不通, explained Tçǔjezu, lack of communication or passage. Communicação is one printed word, not OCR com municação.
Farubaru futçǔni ma- begins a formula about a long lapse in contact. The context favors a temporal separation rather than only physical distance.

runs.text: Ha muito que não nos cõ-

lines.note: Completes macari ſugui ſoro, a polite expression of time elapsed without communication. The printed ſoro is retained without supplying long-vowel marks.
Completes the Portuguese 'we have not communicated or visited'. S. remains an italic register label rather than Japanese text.

runs.text: Erua com que ſe dão botoens de fogo

lines.note: Futçu is the plant used for moxibustion, explained as applying small fire buttons. The next lines connect it with yomogi and rice cakes.
The italic X. is a label. Futçumochi then names rice cakes made with the plant; it is not part of the Portuguese explanation.

runs.text: roz feitos com esta erua. No Cami ſe diz

lines.note: Completes rice cakes made with this herb and introduces the Cami regional name. Cami is italic in this scan and is not mechanically made Roman.
The whole Yomogui is italic, correcting the OCR's mixed Roman initial. It identifies the plant as yomogi; the gui spelling must be read gi, not gwi.
The enlarged worn character and repeated formation support Futçufutçuto, not OCR Futçifutçuto. The sense is clean or decisive cutting.
The repeated adverb also describes answering resolutely. Historical reſpõder and reſolutamente are retained in the Portuguese gloss.
Futçugǒ, explained Tçugǒxezu, describes nonconformity or things not fitting together. Xe is the historical spelling of se, not an OCR substitution.
Completes one thing not fitting another. The sense is incompatibility, not merely a subjective inconvenience inferred from modern usage.
Futçumochi refers back to futçu. The Japanese cross-reference is visibly italic within the Latin Vide instruction and remains as printed.
Futçuqi is the poetic name for the seventh month, explained Xichiguat and 7. Lũa. P. is italic and the final-t spelling is retained.

runs.text: Adu. Modo de cortar cerce, ou

lines.note: Futçuto describes cutting cleanly, the unreduplicated counterpart to Futçufutçuto. Adu. is an italic grammatical label.
Adds answering resolutely. The Portuguese line is a continuation of the adverb's definition, not a new entry.
Fute, tçuru, eta concerns obstinacy or indifference. The scan has a gap in ou não, unlike the joined OCR form.
The example is Futete iru, remaining obstinate, not OCR Furete tru. The headword and enlarged letters support both corrected consonants.

runs.text: obſtinado, & pertinaz ſem ter deuer com

lines.note: The gloss describes obstinacy and pertinacity. The visible b corrects OCR ooſtinado to obſtinado; no s-length normalization is imposed.
Completes disregard for counsel or anything else. Deuer here expresses regard or obligation rather than an isolated financial debt.
Fǔtei names customary manner. Final Xǔ begins a compound across the line break; the scan shows a marked u, not OCR Xi plus period.

Xǔjùno fǔteini xitagatte is following each sect's customary manner. Restore fǔteini from the visible headword repetition and letters; retain the weak mark in jù as printed, and correct Portuguese cui- to cus-.
Completes costume and 'the manner of each sect'. This confirms the sect-custom interpretation of the divided Japanese phrase.
Futen is the encompassing sky, explained Amaneqi ſora and Ten. The Japanese explanatory phrase is italic in the source; retain its typography rather than assume every Japanese token must be Roman.
Completes ceo vniuerſal, the sky encompassing everything. Ceo is historical Portuguese spelling.
Futeqi is boldness with pride and obstinacy, corresponding to the sense of 不敵. The gloss is not merely physical fearlessness.
Futeqina gives the adjectival form, audacious and proud. The example Fute- continues below.
Completes futeqina coto, an audacious or presumptuous act. The Portuguese al- continues as altiuez.
Completes altiuez. This short ending belongs to the example's gloss, not furniture.
Futo, glossed Futto, means suddenly or unexpectedly. The worn final o corrects OCR Futn; the unaccented form is distinct from Futǒ below.
Completes 'outside what one expected'. Cuidaua has the sense of thinking or expecting, not only caring.
Futǒ describes lack of refinement or polish. Policia is cultivated manners here, not a police force.
Futobara and futofara name a horse's belly. The b/f alternatives are explicitly printed and should not be collapsed to one modern spelling.
Futocoro is the bosom. Futocorodeuo ſuru introduces keeping the hands inside the garment rather than an abstract emotional meaning.
Nuqi iredeuo ſuru gives an alternative expression. The Portuguese starts placing the hands in the bosom.
Completes the action through the sleeves. This confirms the clothing-related interpretation of the Japanese expressions.
Futocuxin, explained Cocoroyezu, means not understanding or accepting. The negative -zu is part of the explanation, not the headword.

runs.text: ou não ſe fazer capaz. ¶ Algũas vezes

lines.note: The Portuguese continues with inability to comprehend, then adds a second evaluative sense. Algũas is retained according to the scan-supported baseline.
The secondary sense is unreasonable. Dai futo- begins an emphatic example; the initial syllables are weak but legible in context.
Completes Dai futocuxinna yatçu, an unreasonable fellow. The scan clearly says Duro, not OCR Ouro; the Portuguese is describing a hardheaded person, not gold.
The final word is vilão, correcting truncated OCR oião. It completes the preceding gloss and remains body text above the rule.
Futoi means thick or corpulent. Groſſa and corpulenta establish physical size rather than the later moral sense of futǒ.
Futô is the adverbial form associated with futoi, set on its own indented line. Retain the circumflex, distinct from the later caron-marked forms.
Futoſa is the nominal 'thickness'. Its independent physical line and long ſ are retained.
Futǒjin or futǒna mono describes an ill-bred person. This is the refinement-related futǒ, not the adjective futoi for size.

runs.text: & ſem policia, que reſponde, & não tem

lines.note: The description adds lack of cultivated manners, answering back and having no regard. Policia refers to manners here.
Completes deuer com nada, disregard for anything. The short continuation is fully visible in its crop.
Futojiro is explained Xiroi catabira, a white garment. Restore the missing r in Xiroi and remove the spurious headword space; the scan supports i, rather than a period.
Completes branca and its italic X. label. Catabira in the preceding Portuguese gloss is italic, and is not forced Roman solely because it is Japanese.
Futome is making something large or larger. The principal parts distinguish this transitive verb from futori below.
Futon is explained Xiqimono, a mattress or bedding. The paragraph adds another padded object rather than another headword.

runs.text: Almoſadinha que ſe poem ſobre a ſella do

lines.note: The second sense is a small cushion placed on a horse's saddle. The scan spells ſella with two l letters, correcting the OCR omission.
Completes caualo. This confirms the saddle-cushion sense rather than ordinary sleeping bedding.
Futǒna describes a rustic, ill-bred person. The dictionary's evaluative vocabulary is reported, not adopted as a judgment.

runs.text: que tem pouco medo, & vergonha por mais

lines.note: The person has little fear or shame, however much reprimanded. These are the gloss's social qualities, not physical stoutness.
The scan appears to have quo where syntax expects que; retain it as a possible printed irregularity. Futǒna mono- begins the face example.

runs.text: Se diz de hum que tem focinho

lines.note: Completes mono no tçura, the face of such a person. Focinho carries a disparaging 'mug' sense in the Portuguese gloss.
Completes the ill-bred or low person's appearance. Baixo is social or behavioral in this context, not simply short stature.
Futǒſa and Futǒni are the nominal and adverbial forms. Their open long-o marks remain distinct from Futô under Futoi.
Futoracaxi means making people or animals grow stout. The -acaxi formation is causative, not interchangeable with futori.
The gloss specifies humans and animals growing. Crecer is preserved without modern spelling correction.
Futori is becoming thick or growing. The abbreviated u and otta remain as printed rather than expanded into full modern forms.
Futtçuto means wholly or decisively. The example begins across the line boundary, so Fut- is not another headword.
Completes Futtçuto ijqitta, resolutely refusing. Ijqitta is the historical printed spelling for saying decisively, not a modern ji sequence.
Futtçuto chinuo torazuua vataſumai- concerns refusing passage without receiving a fare. Chin is the charge, and -zuua expresses the negative condition.

runs.text: Diz que não ha de paßar to-

lines.note: Completes to mǒſu and starts the translation of the refusal. The clipped line division is retained; no modern reshaping of vataſumai is applied.

runs.text: talmente ſelhe não dão fretes, ou pagão.

lines.note: The refusal holds unless freight or payment is given. Fretes and pagão express the monetary condition of the Japanese sentence.
Futtei, explained Socouo farǒ, means complete exhaustion or using up. The literal bottom-clearing expression supports that sense.
The sake and rice example illustrates supplies being exhausted. Both are Japanese nouns in the Roman example, not italic Portuguese loanwords here.
Completes futtei icaita, with historical -caita, and begins the gloss that wine and rice are finished. The unusual spelling is not automatically modernized.
Completes acabado, exhausted or finished. The entire short line is retained as a continuation.
Futto repeats the sudden or unexpected sense. Adu. remains italic and the unaccented o is distinct from Futǒ.
Fǔ-v is wind and rain, explained Caje, ame. Restore the visible long-u mark with NINJAL support; the internal hyphen distinguishes the adjacent vowels and is not a line break.
Fuua means discord, explained Yauaragazu and Varui naca. The two u letters bridge fu plus wa and should not be collapsed.
Fuuani naru means a friendship breaking down. The Portuguese inimizade continues from the preceding physical line.
Completes amizade, the object of the breaking. This confirms an interpersonal rather than material rupture.
Fuuagǒ, explained Vagǒxezu, means failure to mix or unite. The following material example precedes a figurative marital use.

runs.text: vnir, como hũ metal com outro, &c. ¶ Itẽ,

lines.note: The material example is one metal failing to unite with another. The paragraph then introduces the metaphorical extension.
Permet is the close-set per met. label introducing a figurative use, not a Japanese word. The definition gives marital disunion.
Completes husband and wife. Molher is the historical spelling and should not be modernized to mulher.

runs.text: Couſas que não ſe miſturão, nem

lines.note: Fuuagǒna describes things that do not mix or unite. The adjective applies to the literal and figurative senses established above.
Meuoto fuuagǒni gozaru says the spouses are not in harmony. The Portuguese starts Aquelles across the line break.

runs.text: quelles caſados não estão amigos, nẽ vnidos.

lines.note: Completes that the spouses are neither friends nor united. Nẽ is retained rather than silently expanded to nem.

runs.text: Estar quebrado na amizade cõ outro.

lines.note: Fuuana describes a broken friendship with another. It is related to Fuua and not a repetition to delete.
The scan separates Fǔ vn, wind and clouds, with a visible space. Preserve the marked u and italic S. register label.
Fuun is ill fortune, explained Facobazu and Vnno nai. The unmarked form contrasts with the weather word above; these are not interchangeable accent variants.
Fuun xigocuna is extreme bad luck. Xigocu is shigoku; the Portuguese mofina here means misfortune, not a personal name.
The final word is deſdita, with long ſ omitted by OCR. It completes the ill-fortune gloss; Fuvn beneath it is separate catchword furniture.
